correctness.rationale: The OU model has K_d=diag(a_i)+dL and stationary covariance solving K_d C+C K_d=Q. Independently solved the exact three-by-three Lyapunov system for path rates (2,1,3), Q=(8,1,1), reproducing the numerator 180d^5+1824d^4+6021d^3+8209d²+4764d+960 and denominator (6d²+17d+6)(12d³+80d²+129d+60). Independent differentiation gives degree-eight P signs ++++----+ and V′=−P/positive denominator², with P(0)>0,P(1/10)<0,P(3)>0. Descartes gives at most two positive roots and IVT gives two, so exactly local minimum and maximum; strict sign witnesses persist on an open six-parameter neighborhood. For n=2 the derived quadratic derivative coefficients change signs at strictly ordered A/B thresholds (a/b)^2,a/b,(3a+b)/(a+3b), allowing at most one positive root; n=1 constant. Thus 3 is sharp in stated model; root decimals alone are not proof.
